title: Chromatic Lens Workshop
description: An antique camera sits on a pedestal beside a prismatic dispersion test object. The user manipulates custom shader parameters on both objects—adjusting chromatic aberration, refraction index, fresnel intensity, and spectral separation—to match a target visual reference. An undo/redo system tracks all parameter changes, and a conservation law ensures total light energy across RGB channels remains constant.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads AntiqueCamera.glb and DispersionTest.glb via GLTFLoader. Place the antique camera on the left and the dispersion test object on the right on a dark reflective plane. Use OrbitControls for scene navigation. Implement custom ShaderMaterial on both models: the camera gets a chromatic aberration post-process style shader with uniforms for aberrationStrength (0-1) and fresnelPower (0.5-5.0); the dispersion object gets a refraction shader with uniforms for refractionIndex (1.0-2.5), spectralSeparation (0-0.1), and dispersionIntensity (0-1). Add a sixth coupled uniform called energyBudget (fixed at 3.0) representing total light energy: whenever any RGB channel gain is adjusted on either object, the other channels auto-compensate so R+G+B always equals energyBudget (conservation law). Provide a floating HTML/CSS control panel with sliders for all six parameters plus three RGB channel gain sliders. Clicking on either model selects it (outline highlight via emissive boost) and the panel targets that model's shader. Implement full undo/redo: store each parameter change as a state snapshot in a history stack, bind Ctrl+Z for undo and Ctrl+Shift+Z for redo, and show undo/redo buttons in the panel. Display a small target reference thumbnail (a canvas with predetermined shader values rendered once) in the corner; the user's goal is to match both objects' appearance to the reference by adjusting all parameters across both models. Show a similarity percentage comparing current uniforms to target values. Add three colored point lights (red, green, blue) orbiting the scene to reveal dispersion and aberration effects dynamically. The interaction requires at minimum: selecting camera (1), adjusting 3 camera params (4), selecting dispersion object (5), adjusting 3 dispersion params (8), tweaking RGB gains with conservation rebalancing (11), plus using undo/redo to correct overshoots. Use HDR-style tone mapping and a dark environment.
